limits: Confirmed prototype defect: one large projected face differs by 1.24 degrees across its domain. Centroid sampling has no justified domain/error bound. The source already requires a faithful derivative or covered approximation.
The proposed failure rule is clear. The prototype's 64-epsilon guard lacks a demonstrated rotational uncertainty bound and a quantified native diagnostic.
Confirmed shared prototype defect: a valid CRS name containing COORDINATEMETADATA is mistaken for a deferred epoch wrapper. Capability detection must use WKT structure, not quoted text.
Retained-variant and unloaded-payload controls pass, including detection of a stale empty claim. This is not a production validator for every composition or variant combination.

Python and C++ share PROJ and external-data decoding. Omniverse reuses Python. General material/primvar baking, physics and nonlinear continuous space/time certificates remain unverified or visibly unsupported.
review_choices: Review finite transport in the instancer frame, including the inverse requirement. It preserves Core input meaning.
Review the explicit Cartesian project context for absolute-domain adjustments. Geographic and global analytical access remain in scope.
Review the proposed publishing-profile identity and maintenance obligations in existing Profiles metadata. Registration and group adoption remain pending.
Review the intermediate-pose policy and physical 3D versus horizontal surface metrics. HPR and detailed WKT string normalization remain proposed.

examples.name: Colorado_02
examples.label: Colorado: State Plane to site grid

opening: USD describes a 3D model's shape and size. Geospatial information says where it belongs on Earth, so models, surveys and measurements can work together.
assessment: Proposal quality means that another implementer can derive the inputs, evaluation order and observable outcomes without guessing. The full draft specifies those rules for the workflows shown here.
summary: Selected demonstrations support the proposed behavior. Detailed conventions still need group review, and three prototype limitations remain. This evidence does not establish exhaustive completeness or independent geodetic accuracy.

cases.title: A geographic location for a 3D model
cases.question: Can a reader distinguish the model's shape from its location on Earth?
cases.rule: The source records model geometry separately from its absolute origin and physical attitude. WKT supplies the coordinate meaning. Ordinary USD operations express intentional scaling and pivots.
cases.expected: A reader can place the model without treating longitude or latitude as a distance or adding computed results to the source schema.
cases.observed: The source stores position and one heading/pitch/roll tuple. Readers compute the physical pose, coordinate results and projection effects without writing them back.
cases.implication: Inputs-only authoring gives the reader one authority for each meaning. The detailed field and pose conventions remain proposed.
cases.boundary: The illustrated position is an example, not a surveyed Eiffel location. No crs:scale is proposed.

cases.title: One physical place, different coordinates
cases.question: Does changing coordinate systems preserve physical placement?
cases.rule: A CRS conversion expresses the same physical location in different coordinates. The reader derives map convergence and local scale from the authoritative WKT and position.
cases.expected: The coordinate numbers and units can change while the tower stays at the same physical place.
cases.observed: Longitude, latitude and height become map coordinates. The physical site stays the same, while grid north and local scale can differ.
cases.implication: A new coordinate representation has a defined physical meaning. The France and Colorado numerical controls test conversion separately from this illustration.
cases.boundary: It explains the rule and does not verify surveyed Paris placement.
cases.clause_heading: ### Source placement evaluation and transform order

image.alt: Eiffel model remains at the same physical location as its coordinate representation changes

cases.title: Ordinary model adjustments after placement
cases.question: In which coordinates do an author's scale, rotation and translation operate?
cases.rule: Child transforms define the model's local geometry. Geospatial position and attitude place that geometry. The directly bound model's own xformOps then adjust the placed result in a fixed project chart, before conversion to the requested output.
cases.expected: Changing the requested output CRS preserves the same physical adjustment. Child offsets continue to follow the model axes.
cases.observed: The illustration scales by 1.15, rotates 20° and moves 120 m east and 60 m south. It shows adjustments on the directly bound model.
cases.implication: The draft distinguishes project adjustments from model-local child offsets. A numerical control separates those interpretations by 4.222 m.
cases.boundary: The chart and reset conventions remain proposed. Ordinary pivots follow the authored USD stack.

image.alt: Eiffel model moves after ordinary scaling and rotation, with its previous position outlined

cases.title: The same rules in two placement readers
cases.question: Can separate implementations derive the same coordinates from the proposed inputs and rules?
cases.rule: Both readers use the composed source inputs and declared output CRS. Results include declared units and meaningful physical comparison.
cases.expected: Python and C++ resolve the same partner points within the recorded comparison tolerance.
cases.observed: The readers compare 213,243 coordinate results. The maximum measured physical difference is 3.39e-08 m.
cases.implication: These cases support reproducible interpretation of the proposed behavior. Agreement alone cannot establish all rules or all input layouts.
cases.boundary: Both readers use PROJ and share native dataset decoding. Agreement does not establish independent geodetic validation.

cases.title: Ordinary USD geometry for rendering
cases.question: Can a renderer use the result without implementing geospatial evaluation?
cases.rule: An explicit bake resolves georeferencing into ordinary geometry and xformOps in a derived copy. A Cartesian coordinate context preserves location without an active source placement binding.
cases.expected: An ordinary USD renderer displays the derived copy. The source scene retains its authored inputs.
cases.observed: Native Hydra/Storm renders the C++-resolved Eiffel bake. A double-precision origin keeps local geometry small.
cases.implication: The visualization path uses ordinary USD geometry. Reassembly controls confirm that a parent translation and an authored reset keep their USD meaning.
cases.boundary: Ground context is illustrative. The image does not establish surveyed placement or surface-normal accuracy.

image.alt: Native Hydra Storm image of the resolved ordinary USD Eiffel bake

cases.title: Measurements stay paired with their locations
cases.question: Can a native measurement dataset remain usable without rewriting values or guessing coordinate meaning?
cases.rule: The scene identifies the native asset, field and coordinate domain. Resolution preserves the pairing of values, locations, missing-data masks and observation times.
cases.expected: A measurement stays the same whether its location is returned geographically or in Earth-centred Cartesian coordinates.
cases.observed: The global field returns geographic and Earth-centred positions for 154 samples, preserving native values and two observation times.
cases.implication: The same data model supports global analytics as well as rendering. Named-dimension controls check the value/location association separately.
cases.boundary: Synthetic temperatures in kelvin. Both readers share decoding, so their agreement alone cannot verify the association.

image.alt: Synthetic global temperature values at their recorded geographic locations

cases.title: A construction site's own survey grid
cases.question: Can a project's local survey grid participate as a defined CRS?
cases.rule: The source WKT describes how a calibrated site grid relates to a broader CRS, including its units and height meaning.
cases.expected: Partner survey lines resolve into the site grid without redefining the model units or up direction.
cases.observed: The original LandXML survey breaklines resolve and reach an ordinary USD bake rendered by Storm.
cases.implication: The partner case exercises a site's calibrated CRS. Its WKT-carried calibration participates in resolution.
cases.boundary: The survey-line image does not establish independent survey accuracy or a continuous terrain-surface certificate.

image.alt: Native Storm render of Colorado survey breaklines in the calibrated site grid

cases.title: Horizontal railway placement
cases.question: Can incomplete source metadata still support a useful, explicitly horizontal workflow?
cases.rule: The reader resolves a declared horizontal association and preserves uninterpreted third components. It does not invent a height reference.
cases.expected: The horizontal railway copy resolves into UTM 32 while the original GeoJSON remains unchanged.
cases.observed: The horizontal copy resolves 15,822 vertices across 2,386 parts. The plot uses offsets only for display.
cases.implication: The draft supports horizontal resolution without inventing a height reference. The original third components remain uninterpreted.
cases.boundary: Horizontal coordinates only. The original third components remain uninterpreted and supply no physical 3D distance.

image.alt: Resolved UTM 32 horizontal railway coordinates with display-only offsets

cases.title: Animation evaluation order
cases.question: Does the proposal define the result between authored moments?
cases.rule: Interpolate the authored source position first, then convert coordinates. Physical orientation uses composed heading/pitch/roll samples and shortest-arc pose interpolation.
cases.expected: The midpoint follows the source-defined path. An ambiguous half-turn requires an intermediate authored pose for interior-time evaluation.
cases.observed: Equatorial longitude changes from 0° to 2°. Interpolating converted endpoints misses the source-first midpoint by 971.421 m.
cases.implication: The order is testable. Sample keys alone cannot certify the original trajectory between samples.
cases.boundary: The bake preserves time codes 0, 5 and 10 at 48 time codes per second. Continuous trajectory coverage remains unverified.

input_rows: Shape and local distances, with declared units and up direction. In USD: points, metersPerUnit and upAxis.
A CRS binding refers to WKT, the standard text description of the location's axes, units and height meaning.
crs:position locates the model origin. The illustrative example uses longitude 2.2945°, latitude 48.8584° and ellipsoidal height 80 m.
crs:orientation records heading, pitch and roll in degrees: which way the model faces and tilts against local east, north and up.
status_rows: The draft separates authored inputs from computed results and defines placement, adjustment, query and bake behavior.
The detailed orientation, frame, WKT string normalization and publication conventions remain proposed.
Lighting directions lack an error bound. Rotation uncertainty is unquantified. A quoted CRS name causes false rejection.
Selected workflows and distinguishing controls support the rules. Broader composition and continuous space/time coverage remain unverified.
placement_choice_rows: One heading/pitch/roll tuple describes physical attitude against local east, north and up. Projection effects stay computed.
The directly bound model's own xformOps adjust its placed result in a fixed project chart, including ordinary pivots.
Child transforms define model-local geometry. Their offsets follow model axes and the geospatial attitude.
Each instance offset retains its instancer-local meaning. Independent prototype placement participates once. A required unavailable inverse fails.
Geographic queries retain longitude/latitude/height. Cartesian geometry and bounds use the datum's Earth-centred frame.
data_choice_rows: Declare the asset, field and coordinate domain. Preserve named dimensions and observation times.
Normalize lexical spelling without losing represented information. Equal tokens establish serialized identity.
Different normalized texts can represent equivalent CRSs. Comparison names its criteria and domain.
Existing Profiles metadata carries a proposed complete publication summary, including unloaded and retained variant content.
Retain a Cartesian CRS and double-precision origin without an active source placement binding. Ordinary USD controls subsequent transforms.
evidence_rows: 213,243 coordinate results per reader. Maximum measured difference 3.39e-08 m. Shared PROJ and decoding.
Reuses Python placement. Readback covers 177,872 vertices and 48 edit, failure and recovery checks across 39 jobs.
Two selected ordinary USD bakes reach native rendering using C++-resolved placements.
113 contract tests and 65 distinguishing controls pass. Separate diagnostics expose the reported prototype limits.
Original inputs and 47 frozen execution files remain unchanged. The immutable receipt identifies exact executed content.
11 selected exports checked. No general material/primvar, physics or continuous trajectory conformance is claimed.
